questions.questionEn: Why does the painted room seem to share the friars' light?

options.textEn: Painted lamps match the lamps on the table.
The wall lets real daylight through the figures.
Light in the scene matches light from the real windows.

questions.hintJa: 明るい場所がどちら側に寄っているかを考えよう。
questions.correctExplanationJa: 絵の主光源は旧食堂の左側からの採光とそろう。それで絵の食卓と実際の部屋が地続きに見える。
questions.incorrectExplanationJa: 主光源は卓上のランプでも人物を透かす仕掛けでもない。 絵の主光源は旧食堂の左側からの採光とそろう。それで絵の食卓と実際の部屋が地続きに見える。

sources.title: A powerful theatrical machine
sources.claimJa: 絵の主光源は旧食堂の左側からの採光とそろう。それで絵の食卓と実際の部屋が地続きに見える。

A2.questionEn: Why does the room in the painting seem to have the same light as the friars' room?

options.textEn: The painted lamps look the same as the lamps on the table.
Real daylight comes through the wall and the people in the painting.
The light in the painting goes the same way as the light from the real windows.

B2.questionEn: What makes the painted room appear to be lit by the very same light as the friars' refectory?

options.textEn: The lamps depicted in the scene correspond to the lamps set on the table.
The wall allows genuine daylight to filter through the figures.
The illumination within the scene is consistent with the light entering through the actual windows.

questions.questionEn: Matthew reaches toward Jesus but looks away. What does this show?

options.textEn: He is asking others to notice what Jesus said.
He is calling a servant to clear the table.
He is turning to see who entered the room.

questions.hintJa: 人の顔の向きと、腕が指す先を別々に見よう。
questions.correctExplanationJa: 館はマタイが隣の使徒たちに、いま聞いた言葉への注意を促す姿と解説する。腕と顔が別々の相手を結ぶ。
questions.incorrectExplanationJa: 配膳の指示や入室者への振り向きとは解説されていない。 館はマタイが隣の使徒たちに、いま聞いた言葉への注意を促す姿と解説する。腕と顔が別々の相手を結ぶ。

sources.title: A powerful theatrical machine
sources.claimJa: 館はマタイが隣の使徒たちに、いま聞いた言葉への注意を促す姿と解説する。腕と顔が別々の相手を結ぶ。

A2.questionEn: Matthew puts his hands out toward Jesus, but he looks the other way. What does this show?

options.textEn: He is asking the others, 'Did you hear what Jesus said?'
He is calling a servant to take the plates away.
He is turning to see who came into the room.

B2.questionEn: Matthew stretches out his arms towards Jesus while turning his gaze elsewhere. What does this gesture convey?

options.textEn: He is urging the others to take note of what Jesus has just said.
He is summoning a servant to clear the table.
He is turning round to see who has come into the room.

questions.questionEn: What freedom did painting on dry plaster give Leonardo?

options.textEn: He could move the wall after painting.
He could work slowly and revise his work.
He could paint the picture without light.

questions.hintJa: 制作する人にとっての時間を考えてみよう。
questions.correctExplanationJa: 乾いた壁に描くことで時間をかけて変更を加えられた。じっくり選んだ一筆には、技法上の理由もある。
questions.incorrectExplanationJa: 壁を移動したり、光なしで描いたりするための選択ではない。 乾いた壁に描くことで時間をかけて変更を加えられた。じっくり選んだ一筆には、技法上の理由もある。

sources.title: The Last Supper
sources.claimJa: 乾いた壁に描くことで時間をかけて変更を加えられた。じっくり選んだ一筆には、技法上の理由もある。

A2.questionEn: Leonardo painted on dry plaster. What did this let him do?

options.textEn: He could move the wall after he painted it.
He could work slowly and change his work.
He could paint the picture with no light.

B2.questionEn: Working on dry plaster, rather than wet, afforded Leonardo what kind of freedom?

options.textEn: The freedom to relocate the wall once it had been painted.
The freedom to proceed at a leisurely pace and revise as he went.
The freedom to paint without any light whatsoever.
